Speed bands 4-5 throughout.' Its justifies_reroute flag is false. The driver's assertion that 'PIE was slow' is therefore backed by no traffic data at all, and POL-RD-23 requires such data before a reroute is justified.

The driver's defence - that he 'messaged the passenger and she said ok' - is not corroborated by the record. The chat log is IMPAIRED: status IMPAIRED, weight_multiplier 0.6, issue code TRUNCATED_LOG (2 of 4 entries exported; nothing after the pickup). That figure is carried in the fare ledger's derived money block and the rider claims it in full; it is the whole of the excess distance fare, which is the measure POL-RD-24 gives the rider on a non-justified deviation.

The rider still carries the disputed charge. The fare ledger shows payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00 and total_charged 17.81, so nothing has been returned and the 0.94 the deviation added is still on the rider's side of the ledger. The rider is the filing party, so under POL-GEN-03 the outcome that leaves the rider not carrying the disputed amount is the PARTIAL_REFUND of the excess distance fare.

This case is one the AI decides and decides as a money refund, not a referral upward. The contested amount is 3.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD threshold, so the AI ruling is final at any confidence; both profiles carry fraud_flags 0, so no 0.95 confidence uplift applies; and POL-RD-25's 2 km ceiling is not in force because thresholds.ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false (in any event 1.30 km is under 2 km). claims.text: The rider asks for 3.00 SGD, but the policy's own arithmetic caps any route-deviation refund at the excess distance fare, and on this record that is 0.94 SGD: POL-RD-24 defines the figure as the deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, with no surge applied, and 1.30 km x 0.72 SGD/km rounds to 0.94 SGD — exactly the figure the payments ledger's own derived money block returns. No row of the POL-RD-24 matrix refunds more than the excess distance fare (rows (b) and (d) refund exactly it, rows (a), (c) and (e) refund nothing), so the rider's claim fails as to at least the remaining 2.06 SGD however the row is chosen.

The rider's 3.00 SGD figure implies roughly 4.2 km of excess distance at the applicable 0.72 SGD/km rate, yet the platform's recorded distances show a deviation of only 1.30 km (13.1 km actual minus 11.8 km recommended), and POL-RD-22 fixes that measurement and expressly bars re-measuring it from the sparse GPS trace because a sparse trace understates a route's length. On the policy's own measure the rider is over-claiming by roughly a factor of three.

Even where a refund is owed, POL-RD-24 refunds the excess distance fare and nothing else: the 2.80 SGD base fare, the 4.68 SGD time fare, the 0.90 SGD platform fee and the 8.49 SGD of distance fare attributable to the kilometres the rider actually travelled are charges for service actually rendered, and the formula carries no surge, no waiting-time and no time component. There is no basis in the policy for the rounder sum the rider demands, and the metered total of 17.81 SGD was correctly charged for the 13.1 km and 26 minutes of service delivered.

No adverse inference can be drawn from the absence of a route message in the chat record. That artifact is impaired — it is truncated (issue code TRUNCATED_LOG, weight multiplier 0.6), carrying only 2 of the 4 entries the trip record counts and both of those sent before the rider boarded at 16:52:25 — so the during-trip exchange the driver describes is missing from the export rather than contradicted by it, and POL-GEN-26 forbids inferring an outcome from the absence of evidence. The record itself shows no call recording exists at all, so nothing before the judge shows the driver failed to inform the rider.

If the judge treats the notification element of POL-RD-21 as bearing on which row of the POL-RD-24 matrix governs, that element cannot be established on this record and the fallback is a human reviewer, not a refund: POL-RD-21 requires the chat log or a recorded call, the chat log is impaired (TRUNCATED_LOG, weight multiplier 0.6) with its during-trip entries absent, and no call recording is in the record, so notice, acknowledgment or their absence are alike unprovable. POL-GEN-26 names 'whether the driver notified the rider' among the facts that escalate the case, and on escalation the charge is held rather than refunded pending that review.

To the rider: your account of the route is borne out and you are owed part of what you asked. To the driver: the record does not support the traffic reason you gave, and the refund follows from the policy's own matrix.

What happened (POL-RD-22, POL-RD-21). The recommended route was PIE to the CTE, via Braddell Road and Bishan Road, 11.8 km. The trip record (EV-TRIP-05019) shows the vehicle leaving the recommended route at the PIE / Adam Road exit at 17:04:15 and rejoining at Bishan Road / Braddell Road at 17:16:09, and the driver's trace (EV-GPS-05019) places it on Adam Road and Thomson Road across that whole stretch. On the platform's recorded distances, which POL-RD-22 makes the measure, 13.1 km actual minus 11.8 km recommended gives a deviation of 1.30 km, against the 1.0 km tolerance. The deviation is established and it is over tolerance; the GPS trace is not used to re-measure it.

Was the reroute traffic-justified (POL-RD-23)? No. The only traffic data in the record is the LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-05019-01). Its type is NONE, which is not one of the closure, congestion or incident types POL-RD-23 and the policy's traffic_justification_types name, its message reads that no incident, roadwork or closure was recorded for the queried segment and window, and its justifies_reroute flag is false. The driver's statement that 'PIE was slow' is an assertion with no traffic data behind it, and POL-RD-23 says such an assertion does not justify a reroute.

Which row applies (POL-RD-24)? Not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km: row (d). It refunds the excess distance fare in full, and that is the whole of what the policy gives on this matrix. Notification is not an element of row (d), so the driver's reliance on having 'messaged the passenger' does not change the row, and the truncated chat export (EV-CHAT-05019, IMPAIRED, weight 0.6, issue code TRUNCATED_LOG) is not needed to decide it. The impaired chat log does not carry the deciding facts here and does not lower the confidence.

The amount (POL-RD-24, POL-GEN-03). The excess distance fare is the deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge, rounded to the cent: 1.30 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 0.94 SGD, the same figure the payments ledger's own derived money block returns (EV-FARE-05019). The rider asked for 3.00 SGD, which implies roughly 4.2 km of excess distance at that rate; the recorded deviation is 1.30 km, so the claim succeeds only to 0.94 SGD. The remaining 2.06 SGD is not supported: the base fare, time fare, platform fee and the distance fare for the kilometres actually travelled are charges for service delivered, and the formula carries no other component. The fare ledger shows payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 (EV-FARE-05019), so nothing has yet been returned and the ruling is a PARTIAL_REFUND of 0.94 SGD. Because the rider filed, the outcome is read from the rider's claim: the rider is owed less than the 3.00 SGD contested, so this is a partial refund and the driver owes no compensation.

The platform's trip record shows the recommended route via the CTE (11.8 km) and the route actually driven via Adam Road and Thomson Road (13.1 km), a deviation of 1.30 km measured as POL-RD-22 requires (actual minus recommended, from the recorded distances, not re-measured from the sparse GPS trace). POL-RD-23 requires such data before a reroute is traffic-justified, and it says a driver's bare assertion of traffic does not justify one, so the driver's 'PIE was slow' does not satisfy it. The case therefore falls in row (d) of POL-RD-24: not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km — the excess distance fare is refunded in full. ledger.claim: The rider's account is exact and the platform's own record confirms it. The recommended route ran PIE to the CTE, but the trip record shows the vehicle leaving the recommended route at the PIE/Adam Road exit at 17:04:15 and rejoining only at Bishan Road/Braddell Road at 17:16:09, while the driver's trace places the vehicle on Adam Road and then Thomson Road for that whole stretch. On the platform's recorded distances, which POL-RD-22 makes the measure, actual 13.1 km minus optimal 11.8 km gives a deviation of 1.30 km against a 1.0 km tolerance: the deviation is established and it is over tolerance.

The reroute is not traffic-justified. The only traffic data in the record is the LTA advisory, whose type is NONE - not one of the closure, congestion or incident types POL-RD-23 and the policy's traffic_justification_types name - and whose own message reads 'No incident, roadwork or closure recorded for the queried segment and window. Speed bands 4-5 throughout.' Its justifies_reroute flag is false. The driver's assertion that 'PIE was slow' is therefore backed by no traffic data at all, and POL-RD-23 requires such data before a reroute is justified.

The driver's defence - that he 'messaged the passenger and she said ok' - is not corroborated by the record. The chat log is IMPAIRED: status IMPAIRED, weight_multiplier 0.6, issue code TRUNCATED_LOG (2 of 4 entries exported; nothing after the pickup). Its two entries are a pickup-location message and the rider's 'ok 2 min' reply at 16:50, roughly thirteen minutes before the 17:04 deviation and plainly about the meeting point, not the route; the trip record's derived messages_during_trip is empty. On this evidence no notice of the deviation under POL-RD-21 can be shown, and the 'ok' the driver relies on was not consent to a reroute.

Under POL-RD-24 exactly one row applies, and this case falls in row (d): not traffic-justified and deviation over 1 km, so the excess distance fare is refunded in full. Rows (a), (b) and (c) are all unavailable because each requires traffic justification, which the record refutes. Notification is not an element of row (d), so the only dimension of row (d)'s two conditions is settled by the trip record and the advisory, and no fact the row needs is missing - POL-GEN-26 is therefore not engaged and this case is decided, not escalated.

The sum row (d) refunds is fixed by the policy's own arithmetic: the deviation distance of 1.30 km times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd of 0.72, without surge, rounded to the cent, gives an excess distance fare of 0.94 SGD. That figure is carried in the fare ledger's derived money block and the rider claims it in full; it is the whole of the excess distance fare, which is the measure POL-RD-24 gives the rider on a non-justified deviation.

The rider still carries the disputed charge. The fare ledger shows payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00 and total_charged 17.81, so nothing has been returned and the 0.94 the deviation added is still on the rider's side of the ledger. The rider is the filing party, so under POL-GEN-03 the outcome that leaves the rider not carrying the disputed amount is the PARTIAL_REFUND of the excess distance fare.

This case is one the AI decides and decides as a money refund, not a referral upward. The contested amount is 3.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD threshold, so the AI ruling is final at any confidence; both profiles carry fraud_flags 0, so no 0.95 confidence uplift applies; and POL-RD-25's 2 km ceiling is not in force because thresholds.ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false (in any event 1.30 km is under 2 km). Nothing here sends the rider to a human reviewer to hold the money.

The rider asks for 3.00 SGD, but the policy's own arithmetic caps any route-deviation refund at the excess distance fare, and on this record that is 0.94 SGD: POL-RD-24 defines the figure as the deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, with no surge applied, and 1.30 km x 0.72 SGD/km rounds to 0.94 SGD — exactly the figure the payments ledger's own derived money block returns. No row of the POL-RD-24 matrix refunds more than the excess distance fare (rows (b) and (d) refund exactly it, rows (a), (c) and (e) refund nothing), so the rider's claim fails as to at least the remaining 2.06 SGD however the row is chosen.

The rider's 3.00 SGD figure implies roughly 4.2 km of excess distance at the applicable 0.72 SGD/km rate, yet the platform's recorded distances show a deviation of only 1.30 km (13.1 km actual minus 11.8 km recommended), and POL-RD-22 fixes that measurement and expressly bars re-measuring it from the sparse GPS trace because a sparse trace understates a route's length. On the policy's own measure the rider is over-claiming by roughly a factor of three.

Even where a refund is owed, POL-RD-24 refunds the excess distance fare and nothing else: the 2.80 SGD base fare, the 4.68 SGD time fare, the 0.90 SGD platform fee and the 8.49 SGD of distance fare attributable to the kilometres the rider actually travelled are charges for service actually rendered, and the formula carries no surge, no waiting-time and no time component. There is no basis in the policy for the rounder sum the rider demands, and the metered total of 17.81 SGD was correctly charged for the 13.1 km and 26 minutes of service delivered.

No adverse inference can be drawn from the absence of a route message in the chat record. That artifact is impaired — it is truncated (issue code TRUNCATED_LOG, weight multiplier 0.6), carrying only 2 of the 4 entries the trip record counts and both of those sent before the rider boarded at 16:52:25 — so the during-trip exchange the driver describes is missing from the export rather than contradicted by it, and POL-GEN-26 forbids inferring an outcome from the absence of evidence. The record itself shows no call recording exists at all, so nothing before the judge shows the driver failed to inform the rider.

If the judge treats the notification element of POL-RD-21 as bearing on which row of the POL-RD-24 matrix governs, that element cannot be established on this record and the fallback is a human reviewer, not a refund: POL-RD-21 requires the chat log or a recorded call, the chat log is impaired (TRUNCATED_LOG, weight multiplier 0.6) with its during-trip entries absent, and no call recording is in the record, so notice, acknowledgment or their absence are alike unprovable. POL-GEN-26 names 'whether the driver notified the rider' among the facts that escalate the case, and on escalation the charge is held rather than refunded pending that review.
